column31: At a willingness-to-pay of $50,000/QALY and a ciNPWT unit price of $250, ciNPWT is cost-effective in any patient whose predicted 90-day SSI risk exceeds 1.335%. At that risk ciNPWT prevents 5.19 SSIs per 1,000 patients treated (NNT 193).

At a willingness-to-pay of $100,000/QALY and a ciNPWT unit price of $250, ciNPWT is cost-effective in any patient whose predicted 90-day SSI risk exceeds 1.235%. At that risk ciNPWT prevents 4.80 SSIs per 1,000 patients treated (NNT 208).

At a willingness-to-pay of $150,000/QALY and a ciNPWT unit price of $250, ciNPWT is cost-effective in any patient whose predicted 90-day SSI risk exceeds 1.149%. At that risk ciNPWT prevents 4.47 SSIs per 1,000 patients treated (NNT 224).

Ignoring QALYs entirely, ciNPWT pays for itself in pure payer dollars at a predicted 90-day SSI risk of 1.453% and above; below that it still buys health, but it costs money to do so. This is the most conservative of the four risk thresholds -- it is the number to quote to a payer who declines to price QALYs. At that risk ciNPWT prevents 5.65 SSIs per 1,000 (NNT 177).

The same threshold computed without discounting and without the half-cycle correction: 1.219%. It reproduces the engine's published 1.219% and sits just above the price-year-consistent hand calculation 1.215% (p* = C / [(1 - RR) x (SSI cost + WTP x QALY loss)]). Discounting raises the threshold because the device toll falls at cycle 0, where the discount factor is exactly 1, while every benefit is discounted. Every column on this row is evaluated on the undiscounted basis.

column29: ALL-CAUSE COST SENSITIVITY, not the base case. The six SSI cost tranches are charged at m_ssi_cost = 1.000, i.e. Edmiston [12]'s regression-adjusted ALL-CAUSE payment increment taken at face value, instead of the base case's matched anchor m_ssi_cost = k_attrib_pennington = 0.492 from Pennington [14]. Because an all-cause increment absorbs confounding by indication it is an UPPER bound on attributable cost, so this family reports a LOWER break-even risk than the base case -- ciNPWT appears to pay off sooner. That direction is the whole point of reporting it as a bound rather than as the headline. Solved and evaluated on the REPORTING BASIS (24 cycles, 3%/yr, half-cycle) so it pairs like-for-like with the base-case rows of the same family. Select these rows with family.str.endswith('_attrib').
